lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Look & write

details: Look and write serves as a comprehensive review of the unit's language. Students must analyse the posts to connect the events with the resulting feelings and complete the sentences correctly.
Look for correctly completed sentences in all four posts, showing that students can logically connect the described events and the corresponding feelings.

“Many people like to post online about their day! Not me, I only tell my friends. For example, I’ve got lots of work to do tonight. Can you guess how I feel? That’s right! I feel anxious. Let’s see if you know how these people are feeling”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B Listen and write O or X.

details: Listen and write O or X assesses listening for detail. Students listen to descriptions of events and feelings, and then evaluate whether the pictures are a correct (O) or incorrect (X) match.
Look for correctly written O's and X's in the boxes, demonstrating that students have understood the audio and can evaluate the corresponding pictures.
“I often listen to my friends talking about their day, but I don’t always understand!. Can you help me listen to these  two people? Let’s see if the pictures match what they say!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.91 - A Complete the crossword.

details: Complete the crossword serves as a comprehensive review of the unit's language. Students must complete the clue sentences with the correct verbs and adjectives to solve the puzzle, testing their overall knowledge.
Look for correctly completed clue sentences and a fully and accurately filled crossword grid, demonstrating a strong command of the unit's language.

“It’s my favourite thing - puzzle time! And this time it’s a crossword. I love crosswords. To find the answers, you must first read and complete the clue sentences correctly. Let's see who can solve it first!”

Look for accurately reconstructed sentences with the correct word order, capitalisation, and punctuation for all four items.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Presentation Silly Sentences

details: Silly Sentences is a culminating project that synthesizes the unit's language in a creative game. Students generate random combinations of events and feelings, record them, and present the most humorous results.
Look for active and engaged participation in the game, a correctly filled chart, and a clear, confident presentation of the silly sentences to the class (and a few laughs!).

“Do you think I’m silly? I hope not! But today I will be! Because now we're going to play a game called 'Silly Sentences'! You’ll use your cards to play with your group to make funny combinations. Then you can present the silly sentences your to the class. Let’s see who gets the silliest sentences!”
